title: The Pokemon Game That Was Supposed to Delete Itself Is Back
summary:
A video game that was designed to delete itself has come back to life, 20 years later. The game is PokePark: Fishing Rally, a mini-game for the Nintendo DS that could only be downloaded at a pop-up Pokemon theme park in Nagoya, Japan, in the summer of 2005.

The game was programmed to self-destruct, erasing itself after 12 hours or once the handheld was reset. For years, fans wondered if it would ever be playable again. Now a collector named Daniel Quadri has come into possession of what appears to be the only confirmed fully playable copy, and he confirmed the find to the gaming site IGN.

Quadri said preserving a game like this means so much to him, and that it felt surreal to switch on his DS, spend a quiet moment fishing, and feel the rush of reeling in a Gyarados. For a moment, he said, he got to feel what it must have been like to play it at PokePark in 2005.

At the 2005 park, players could walk around the attraction, which was about the size of a Costco parking lot, and catch water-type Pokemon, a bit like an early version of Pokemon Go. The game could only be downloaded through the DS local wireless features, and later at certain Pokemon Center stores in Japan. Demo builds and online listings have turned up over the years, but Quadri's cartridge, whose source he has not explained, appears to be the only fully playable copy.

Quadri sent his cartridge to the grading company PSA, and he has also said he would like to help preserve Fishing Rally by sharing the file with other DS systems. As he put it, imagine being one of those kids and finding out years later that the game you played that day had become a piece of lost Pokemon history. With this cartridge in his DS, he can recreate that experience today.
why_it_matters: The find shows why saving old games matters: a game that was meant to vanish can become a piece of history, and one surviving copy can let people experience it again.
